_comment: What gets published: one list of packages for the pipeline and the app.
The app reads `app`, `symbol` and `app_detail` through `maps.json`; its own
table (`skifahrer/rikimaps`, `MapPiece.swift`) must match, a test guards both.
key         file stem (`presovsky-terrain.zip`) and key in `maps.json`
app         package name in the app
symbol      SF Symbol the app draws it with
app_detail  one line under the name in the app
description one line for the log, `contents.json` and the catalog
sources     whose data it is: keys of `credits` in map-settings.json, or the source kind the map picked (`dem:contours`, `aerial:summer`)
manifest    keys in `regions.<region>` of `_site/tiles/manifest.json`
suffixes    fallback when the manifest is unreadable: file name endings
origin      `site` = from `_site`, `wiki` = from the `--wiki` folder
regenerate  key that builds it alone (`Map · Regenerate region layer`)
part_of     package it also travels in
optional    manifest keys a region may go without (no traffic sign there) – not an error
rest        also carries what no other package does – styles, sprites, trails, the manifest
legacy      former keys; their old files on Drive are removed on publish
reads       the prefilters (`osmium tags-filter --expressions`) its own schemas read OSM through
owns        the OSM tags it owns: `key` for every value no other package names, `key=a,b` for those
Order is the order in the app. A package dropped from here goes to `retired`,
whose files (key and legacy names) are deleted on Drive. A tag two packages own is listed in
`shared` with the package meant to keep it (`workers/lint/owners.py`); `workers/tools/overlap.py`
measures what a build really shares; `base_map` says where the base map's layers go.

packages.description: the whole OSM cartography – areas, lines, labels, waymarked trails and the offline search index

packages.app_detail: Hillshading and 3D terrain, from the height model
packages.description: terrain height as terrarium tiles (raster .pmtiles) – the client draws hillshading and 3D terrain from it

packages.app_detail: Contour lines from the height model
packages.description: contour lines from the height model (.pmtiles)

packages.app_detail: Cliffs and rock areas, from the terrain's slope
packages.description: rock areas from the slope of the height model or from hillshading (.pmtiles)

packages.app_detail: Aerial photos of the land in summer, under the map
packages.description: orthophoto mosaic taken in summer, as JPEG raster tiles (raster .pmtiles)

packages.app_detail: Aerial photos of the land under snow, under the map
packages.description: orthophoto mosaic taken in winter, as JPEG raster tiles (raster .pmtiles)

packages.app_detail: Land, parks, peaks, landscape lines and airports
packages.description: the base map's land cover and use, protected areas, peaks, ridges and cliffs, airports, and the landscape lines and areas OpenMapTiles lacks – embankments, power lines, fences, walls (.pmtiles)

packages.app_detail: Roads, tracks and ferries, for search and routing
packages.description: the OSM roads a car can drive – motorways to tracks, and ferries – with road limits, traffic signs and their images, house-numbered addresses, the signed routing network the phone routes on, and the base map's roads, their names and house numbers (.pmtiles)

packages.app_detail: Footways, cycleways, steps and via ferratas
packages.description: the OSM ways cars don't fit – footways, paths, cycleways, bridleways, steps, pedestrian streets and via ferratas – with surface, access and how hard a path is, the base map's paths and their signs – and what the region needs drawn at all: styles, sprites, waymarked trails, the manifest (.pmtiles)

packages.app_detail: Marked hiking, cycling and ski routes, in their colours
packages.description: waymarked routes from OSM relations – hiking, cycling, ski, horse routes and via ferratas, with their colour and mark (.pmtiles); a region's base map carries them; a mountain package draws them with its paths
OSM point features – springs, caves, lookouts, monuments – and the base map's points: shops, sights, services (.pmtiles)
OSM boundaries of state, region, district and municipality, with the names of those areas and the base map's borders (.pmtiles)
OSM rivers, streams, lakes, reservoirs and the sea, with their names, and the base map's water (.pmtiles)

packages.app_detail: Railways, trams and cable cars, with stations
packages.description: every OSM railway including those under construction, planned and abandoned, every cable car in service, being built or planned, named stations, line signs and the track network the phone routes trains on, and the base map's rails (.pmtiles)

packages.app_detail: Military, historic and abandoned places, old lifts
packages.description: OSM military sites, historic places and listed monuments, mines, shafts, adits and quarries, and everything abandoned or disused – lifts and cable cars too, railways not – as points, lines and areas (.pmtiles)

packages.app_detail: Cities, villages, mountains, valleys, plains and regions
packages.description: OSM names of cities, towns, villages and settlements, mountain ranges, ridges and peaks, valleys, plains and regions – a layer per kind, points and lines (.pmtiles)

packages.app_detail: Ski areas, pistes, lifts, cable cars and winter paths
packages.description: OSM ski areas, downhill pistes by difficulty, cross-country trails, ski tours, sledging runs, winter paths, every ski lift and the cable cars in the mountains, in service, being built or planned, with their stations – a layer per kind (.pmtiles); a region carries it, and so does a range

packages.app_detail: Buildings and the places they make up
packages.description: every OSM building with floor area in m², name, kind, levels and address, and place names from city to hamlet, and the base map's buildings and places (.pmtiles)

packages.app_detail: Articles, read from a place you tap
packages.description: Wikipedia articles for the region's objects: articles.ndjson + index.json

_comment: Which package each layer of the base map (OpenMapTiles) goes to: `workers/tiles/cut.py` cuts by it,
and the app's `MapOverlay.claimedBaseSourceLayers` must match, a test guards both.
layers  a whole layer to one package
split   a layer shared by its features: `tag`'s value picks the package from `to`, else `else`;
a value in `drop` stays in the whole base map only, its owner draws it from its own archive

shared.why: Settlements and Geographical names both, the app keeps one (rikimaps#2794); Boundaries drops it
role: Landscape the mark, Geographical names the name; Points carries them for a range only, which has no base map
Points carries them for a range only, whose Water draws no points
Railways carries every cable car, Ski & winter those in the mountains (workers/lib/cable_cars.py)
Points carries them for a range only, which has no Army & history
Points carries them for a range only, which has no Army & history
role: Settlements the building, Army & history the ruin's mark
